response.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, structure, containment/owner default-entry, group guard collisions, wrong local-exit targets, and cross-context consistency using exact source and closed-model identities. Key findings: (1) NL3 requires target search -> formation adjustment on interception; the closed model shows source SearchMission -> FormationAdjust (composite level), consistent since target search state is nested within SearchMission and the transition is authored at SearchMission scope, but the actual outgoing edge is only defined at SearchMission (not at the inner Search state) with route-token indirection through Region1's leaf 'Search' consuming Interception_Detected and setting token=9, then SearchMission->FormationAdjust fires on token==9. This realizes the endpoint through the macro/route-token chain from Search (nested) up to SearchMission -> FormationAdjust, which the working contract treats as compiler-owned segments of one macro transition (tr_0009). NL4 similarly: Search consumes Task_Assignment_Received setting token=12, then SearchMission->AttackState fires on token==12 (macro tr_0012). Both endpoints resolve through the protected macro chain, which per protocol should be assessed as a whole rather than flagged per-segment, and the macro closes (all joins present), so no wrong-target candidate is warranted for those. (3) NL2-CARDINALITY and region_structure: the search-task scope authored as three state areas (Region1/Region2/Region3) is realized in FCSTM as three nested composites Region1 > Region2 > Region3, i.e., a nesting hierarchy rather than three sibling/parallel areas, but this is a member-domain binding decision left to cardinality_bindings. (4) FormationAdjust and AttackState composites both contain their required states (AdjustingFormation, Attacking) - containment contracts for NL3-DERIVED and NL4-DERIVED are satisfied by direct containment, so omitted from candidates. (5) Owner-level default entry: SearchMission, FormationAdjust, and AttackState each have exact owner-local initial edges (transition:line:45 Region1's parent SearchMission -> Region1; transition:line:49 FormationAdjust -> AdjustingFormation; transition:line:54 AttackState -> Attacking) that are proved in verify_facts, so no derived initial-entry defect for those owners. (6) The refuted initial-entry checks (transition:line:61 root->SearchMission conditional/unreachable trigger; transition:line:21 Region2->Region3 guarded) are structural anomalies but neither NL contract's owner/target pairing selects those exact scopes explicitly as normative default-entry obligations distinct from what's already covered; however the root entry anomaly (transition:line:61, root [*] -> SearchMission triggered by Start_Mission but unreachable from top-level initial per EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE and INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL diagnostics) is a genuine cross-view structural fact: the machine's own top-level initial pseudostate has no unconditional/default entry into SearchMission (only a Start_Mission-triggered edge that the deterministic facts say is unreachable), which undermines root reachability for the entire NL2 continuously-operating obligation. This is captured as a derived reachability/initial_entry issue anchored on NL2's state_action contract, since NL2 requires continuous operation but the root has no reachable default entry into SearchMission per deterministic facts.

This realizes the endpoint through the macro/route-token chain from Search (nested) up to SearchMission -> FormationAdjust, which the working contract treats as compiler-owned segments of one macro transition (tr_0009). NL4 similarly: Search consumes Task_Assignment_Received setting token=12, then SearchMission->AttackState fires on token==12 (macro tr_0012). Both endpoints resolve through the protected macro chain, which per protocol should be assessed as a whole rather than flagged per-segment, and the macro closes (all joins present), so no wrong-target candidate is warranted for those. (3) NL2-CARDINALITY and region_structure: the search-task scope authored as three state areas (Region1/Region2/Region3) is realized in FCSTM as three nested composites Region1 > Region2 > Region3, i.e., a nesting hierarchy rather than three sibling/parallel areas, but this is a member-domain binding decision left to cardinality_bindings. (4) FormationAdjust and AttackState composites both contain their required states (AdjustingFormation, Attacking) - containment contracts for NL3-DERIVED and NL4-DERIVED are satisfied by direct containment, so omitted from candidates. (5) Owner-level default entry: SearchMission, FormationAdjust, and AttackState each have exact owner-local initial edges (transition:line:45 Region1's parent SearchMission -> Region1; transition:line:49 FormationAdjust -> AdjustingFormation; transition:line:54 AttackState -> Attacking) that are proved in verify_facts, so no derived initial-entry defect for those owners. (6) The refuted initial-entry checks (transition:line:61 root->SearchMission conditional/unreachable trigger; transition:line:21 Region2->Region3 guarded) are structural anomalies but neither NL contract's owner/target pairing selects those exact scopes explicitly as normative default-entry obligations distinct from what's already covered; however the root entry anomaly (transition:line:61, root [*] -> SearchMission triggered by Start_Mission but unreachable from top-level initial per EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE and INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL diagnostics) is a genuine cross-view structural fact: the machine's own top-level initial pseudostate has no unconditional/default entry into SearchMission (only a Start_Mission-triggered edge that the deterministic facts say is unreachable), which undermines root reachability for the entire NL2 continuously-operating obligation. This is captured as a derived reachability/initial_entry issue anchored on NL2's state_action contract, since NL2 requires continuous operation but the root has no reachable default entry into SearchMission per deterministic facts.

response.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, forbidden-scope entry, dead-end/frontier facts, cross-wrapper reachability, and stable termination. Key findings: (1) Start_Mission's only consumer transition (line:61, [*]->SearchMission with trigger Start_Mission) is unreachable from the top-level initial entry per inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics and verify_facts (event-consumer:Start_Mission refuted), which is a behavioral consequence of NL1/NL2's operating-scope obligation that the UAV swarm must operate at all (the machine's own top-level start event has no reachable consumer, though SearchMission itself is reachable via the top-level machine root wrapper state, so this is best captured as a derived event_consumer_coverage issue distinct from the satisfied endpoint contracts). (2) The transition_endpoints contracts for NL3 (Search->FormationAdjust) and NL4 (Search->AttackState, and SearchMission-level Search->AttackState) are satisfied at the SearchMission-level (transitions at line:57 and line:59 exist with correct guards), but the deeper NL3-ENDPOINT-1 and NL4-DERIVED-d11218fc814965e4fae8 contracts name 'target search state' as source, which maps to Search or SearchMission depending on binding; closed model shows Interception_Detected and Task_Assignment_Received are consumed inside Search (deep state, lines 38-41) and propagate via route-token effects up through Region2/Region3/Region1 to SearchMission-level transitions 57/59, which is a valid macro-collapsed routing pattern reaching FormationAdjust/AttackState - endpoints are satisfied. (3) NL4-EFFECT-1 (variable_delta on UAV count decrease) has no S-predicate for variable_delta; the Attacking->[*] transition at line 55 only sets R45RouteToken=14, an internal route-control variable, not any UAV-count variable - no such variable exists in the model at all (working_contract confirms only 1 variable: R45RouteToken, a compiler-owned route_control_variable), so the required effect is entirely absent from the closed model - a clear violation. (4) Termination: the model report lists a final_states entry 'SearchMission.Region1.Search' in canonical IR but the closed FCSTM shows Region3's exit uses InvalidFinaltr_0008 (synthetic, boundary outside ancestry) which then just routes back up via route-token effects to SearchMission - so there is no true termination state; this is relevant to overall model shape but not tied to an explicit termination contract in the supplied NL contracts (no termination-state contract exists here), so omitted per protocol. (5) Cardinality: NL2-CARDINALITY-1 requires exactly 3 state areas for UAV search-task scope; binding produced below.
